title: Steve Jobs at Macworld Boston 1997: refocusing Apple on relevance, core assets and thinking different
summary: Jobs reports on his first four weeks back at a struggling Apple. He diagnoses a missing strategy, not missing talent, and calls for focus on where Apple is still relevant. He announces a new board and the Microsoft partnership, and ends with the "think different" idea of making tools for creative people.

principles.text: A company in trouble often has good people doing the wrong things because the plan is wrong; fix the strategy first.
principles.quote: Apple is executing wonderfully on many of the wrong things organization to execute is really high

principles.text: People will line up behind a clear strategy; chaos usually means no strategy was ever given.
principles.quote: I found people that can't wait to fall into line behind a good strategy there just hasn't been one

principles.text: Focus on where you are still relevant, identify your core assets, and invest more in them.
principles.quote: Apple needs to find where it is still incredibly relevant and focus on those areas it needs to figure out what its core assets are and invest more in them

principles.text: Turnarounds start at the top: change leadership and the board before the lower ranks.
principles.quote: I think this change needs to start at the top with the board of directors

principles.text: Drop the win/lose mindset with competitors and take responsibility for your own results.
principles.quote: we have to let go of this notion that for Apple to win Microsoft has to lose okay we have to embrace a notion that for Apple to win Apple has to do a really good job

principles.text: Build tools for the creative misfits who want to change the world; see genius in what others call craziness.
principles.quote: a lot of times people think they're crazy but in that craziness we see genius and those are the people we're making tools for
